title: BEA state GDP: Q2 2026
gist: BEA's Q2 2026 state data show 2.2% national annualized growth with 44 of 50 states growing; New York led at 4% on finance and insurance, while mining-heavy West Virginia and Wyoming contracted. Q1 revisions were large (Alaska -3.8%, DC 7.3%).

insights.claim: BEA reported Q2 2026 real GDP growth for US states averaging 2.2% annualized, with 44 of 50 states plus Washington, DC growing.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Broad-based expansion at the state level; only six states contracted.

insights.claim: Growth was uneven: median state Iowa grew 1.7%, below the 2.2% national average, and 32 states grew slower than the national average.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: A few fast growers lift the average above the typical state's experience.

insights.claim: The St. Louis Fed's Eighth District states all grew in Q2 but all eight were slower than the national average, with Mississippi and Illinois fastest at 2.1%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Regional lag relevant to regional banks and local credit conditions in the Midwest/Mid-South.

insights.claim: New York grew fastest at 4% annualized, followed by South Carolina and Delaware at 3.5%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog

insights.claim: Finance and insurance were the leading contributors to real GDP growth in New York and Delaware, per BEA.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Financial-sector strength is driving the top-line state outperformance.

insights.claim: Alaska, Kansas, Nebraska, North Dakota, West Virginia and Wyoming contracted in Q2, with West Virginia steepest at -2.3% and Wyoming at -1.6%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Contraction clusters in resource and agricultural states.

insights.claim: Mining was the leading contributor to the GDP decline in West Virginia and Wyoming, per BEA.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Resource-extraction weakness is a regional drag; watch coal and energy-linked state economies.

insights.claim: Q1 2026 state GDP growth revisions averaged roughly +/- 2% across all states and DC, indicating high noise in preliminary state data.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Treat first-release state GDP prints cautiously; annual revision comes the following March.

insights.claim: Alaska's Q1 growth was revised down from 2.8% to -3.8% (largest downward revision), while Washington, DC's was revised up from 2.2% to 7.3% (largest upward).
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Illustrates how a single revision can flip a state from growth to contraction.

insights.claim: FRED's ALFRED database records data vintages, letting users see state GDP as it appeared at earlier dates, which matters given the revision magnitudes.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Use vintage data for backtests to avoid look-ahead bias from revised figures.
insights.locator: Note: These data are subject to future revision
